observation_summary: The ContinuedFraction evaluation algorithm was numerically unstable for large inputs, leading to divergence (NaN/Infinity) and incorrect results in cumulative probability calculations.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves a complete rewrite of the iterative computation logic within the ContinuedFraction.evaluate method. The original implementation used a specific recurrence relation that was prone to overflow/divergence for large inputs. The fix replaces this with a more numerically stable formulation (using scaling and different recurrence variables), which is a classic algorithmic correction to improve numerical stability and correctness.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows a complete replacement of the recurrence variables (cN, q2, dPrev, etc.) and the update logic inside the loop.
The stack trace indicates a ConvergenceException due to the continued fraction diverging to NaN.
The bug report mentions that the method returns wrong values for large trials, indicating a failure in the underlying mathematical computation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not just changing a constant or initialization value; it is a fundamental change to the mathematical recurrence formula used to compute the continued fraction.
While the fix includes checks for zero (using Precision.equals), these are part of the new, more stable algorithm, not just a missing guard for an existing correct procedure.
